extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO and participants in OED disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural outcomes for an Affidavit of Resignation submitted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 (resignation on consent) and the Office's approval/ordering of exclusion from practice. Covers jurisdictional status, scope and effective date of exclusion, and applicability of the USPTO professional conduct rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review and approval of Affidavit of Resignation (37 C.F.R. § 11.27(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(b), the Director of the USPTO received for review and approval from the OED Director an Affidavit of Resignation executed by the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Affidavit of Resignation submitted under § 11.27 must be received by the USPTO Director for review and approval before exclusion on consent is effective. The document submitted here was a two-page Affidavit of Resignation executed February 24, 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Affidavit — exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent submitted an Affidavit of Resignation to the USPTO for the purpose of being excluded on consent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When approved by the Director, an affidavit filed under § 11.27 effectuates exclusion on consent rather than a contested disciplinary determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusion from practice before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be excluded on consent from practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of this Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the exclusion applies to trademark and other non-patent matters; it also notes the respondent is not registered and not otherwise eligible to represent others before the Office in patent matters (i.e., patent practice remains subject to registration requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and practitioner status
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is an attorney admitted to practice in New York, currently active, has practiced before the Office in trademark matters, and is a 'practitioner' pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the Office's jurisdiction to act under its disciplinary rules over the respondent as a practitioner who has practiced before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO professional conduct rules by date
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility, 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq., and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code of Professional Responsibility applies to conduct that occurred prior to May 3, 2013, while the Rules of Professional Conduct apply to conduct occurring on or after May 3, 2013. This temporal allocation determines which standards govern particular conduct at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion on consent becomes effective commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval of the Affidavit by the Director results in immediate exclusion as of the Final Order date; the Order itself states the exclusion commences on that date.
